summary: Embedding header flag dropped by client SDK causing rerank reorder and intermittent latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC Acme Health has reported intermittent rerank quality shifts accompanied by 2-6x latency spikes on their private deployment. The root symptom appears as out-of-order rerank results for the same query vectors across repeated requests and a subset of requests showing CPU fallback with long tail latencies.

Impact: Customer-facing search results for clinical knowledge retrieval are unstable; appears in ~4% of queries during peak load windows, causing degraded UX and an escalation to enterprise support. No data loss, but query latency and ranking correctness are impacted.

Environment: Private deployment (on-prem appliance) behind customer-managed VPC peered to Redwood control plane. TLS terminated at customer edge. Only seen in us-east region on customer's dedicated cluster.

Observed at the customer after upgrading their SDK to v0.18.2. Older SDK (v0.17.x) did not show the problem.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Using customer SDK v0.18.2, call /embeddings with model=redwood-embed-v1, include metadata headers; 2) Immediately call /rerank with the returned embedding batch (same request IDs) in the same TCP session; 3) Repeat the pair of calls ~1000 times at modest concurrency (~10 QPS) and observe that ~3-6% of rerank responses have reordered top-k and elevated latency (>600ms). 4) Repeat with SDK v0.17.9 and observe reproducible absence of the issue.

Notes: Reproducible only when embedding and rerank are done in quick succession without an explicit cache-bust; spacing requests by >1s reduces incidence (likely hiding race/ordering issue).
logs_snippets:
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=abcd123 embedding-service: accept request headers: X-Embed-Dim=128, X-Embed-Format=fp32
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=abcd123 api-gateway: forward to reranker with header X-Embed-Dim missing
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=abcd123 reranker: detected missing dim header, performing compatibility heuristic -> fallback to CPU path (est latency +450ms)
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=abcd123 reranker: computed scores (using heuristic normalization) -> ranks differ from GPU path by top-3 in edge cases
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=efgh456 embedding-service: accept request headers: X-Embed-Dim=128, X-Embed-Format=fp16
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=efgh456 api-gateway: forwarded headers preserved
[2026-03-12T02:41:05Z] req=efgh456 reranker: used GPU path, latency 80ms, ranks stable

Correlation: all affected req ids show drop of X-Embed-Dim header between embedding-service and reranker inside the control-plane HTTP proxy.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: packet/proxy header trimming in the customer's edge or SDK change removed a small, optional header (X-Embed-Dim) used by internal routing to select GPU vs CPU rerank path. Evidence: captured request traces show header present at embedding-service but absent at reranker for impacted requests.

Secondary hypothesis: SDK v0.18.2 introduced a keep-alive/connection reuse optimization which interleaves requests and causes proxy-specific header reuse/overwrite when embedding and rerank are sent on different logical streams. Reproducer: toggling the SDK's keep-alive off reduces incidence.

Action taken so far: 1) Eng SRE mirrored customer traffic in staging appliance to reproduce; 2) Added temporary server-side guard to treat missing X-Embed-Dim as preserved but annotated (logging) to avoid CPU fallback; 3) Requested SDK vendor (client team) to patch header handling.

Open questions: - Is the header removal happening in customer's edge load balancer or in our internal control plane proxy? - Should we make reranker selection solely content-based (vector shape) instead of header-driven to be resilient?
comments:
[2026-03-12] Aisha Patel: Customer reports started after SDK bump to v0.18.2; they provided SDK logs showing keep-alive enabled.
[2026-03-12] Jonah Kim: I've reproduced in staging by enabling the same SDK keep-alive behavior against our private appliance; confirmed header drop on our HA proxy (nginx sidecar) when multiple pipelined requests are present.
[2026-03-13] Mia Torres (SRE): Deployed temporary logging guard to reranker; observed 21 additional requests where header was dropped but fallback avoided, latency reduced from 700ms to 120ms.
[2026-03-14] Engineering: Preparing a targeted patch to tolerate missing header and infer dim from payload for routing. Will follow up with SDK team about a fix in v0.18.3.
resolution:
In progress - temporary mitigation applied (tolerate missing header and infer dims) on customer cluster which reduced CPU fallback incidence by ~90% in trials. Customer notified and given configuration steps to disable SDK keep-alive as an immediate workaround. Permanent fix planned: change reranker routing to detect embedding vector dimensionality from request body when header is absent and land SDK patch to avoid header drop.

Planned rollout: 1) Merge server-side infer-dim patch (PR #842) to staging (target 2026-03-15), 2) Coordinate with customer to test in their private appliance (2026-03-16), 3) Release SDK v0.18.3 with header stability fixes (2026-03-17).
follow_up_actions:
- Engineering: complete PR to infer embedding dims from payload and add idempotent header preservation in control-plane proxy (owner: Jonah Kim).
- SDK: patch connection reuse to preserve optional headers or document and add explicit header-copy behavior (owner: Client SDK team).
- Support: schedule 1:1 with Acme Health PM to validate UX after patch (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Postmortem: write short postmortem and add test coverage for header-preservation race in our e2e tests (owner: Mia Torres).
customer_notes: Customer confirmed that disabling keep-alive reduced errors in an A/B test and is amenable to scheduling a maintenance window for testing the patched server. They asked for an ETA on a permanent fix and requested a follow-up on whether this could affect other private customers.
